texts: Wound complications occur in nearly 10 percent of MIDCAB patients: D.

MIDCAB brings the left internal mammary artery to the LAD through a small left anterior thoracotomy, on the beating heart; the spread ribs bring pain, infection, poor healing and, rarely, lung hernia.
In the picture, one sailor in ten grows green mould round his small hatch.

Early mortality is low, under 1 to 2 percent; graft stenosis at angiography and anastomotic revision are not rarer than after standard CABG, as the anastomosis is sewn through a small opening on a moving heart.
Stroke is not more common after multivessel minimally invasive bypass, which often avoids handling the aorta.
Memory hook: one small hatch in ten grows mould.
